articles.title: GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Actors Spotted Together in First Photo
articles.summary: The actors behind GTA 6 protagonists Jason and Lucia have finally been pictured together, after years of speculation regarding their identities.
articles.body:
The actors behind GTA 6 protagonists Jason and Lucia have finally been pictured together, after years of speculation regarding their identities.

As we learned earlier this week, Lucia is played by Manni L. Perez — though this casting was only confirmed as the actress received a Game Awards nomination for her work.

Now, we can see Jason actor Dylan Rourke revealed and in the flesh too, sharing a hug with Perez and her stunt double Victoria Lee, while standing in front of a giant Grand Theft Auto 6 billboard.

"Well... the secret's finally out!" Lee posted on Instagram today. "After keeping my mouth shut for YEEAARRSSS (and what feels like FOREVER!!! 😂), I can finally share that I've been lucky enough to help bring LUCIA to life as her MAIN STUNT DOUBLE in GRAND THEFT AUTO 6, along with a whole bunch of other characters stunts along the way!"

Lee's photo is the first time we've seen Rourke publicly confirmed to be playing Jason, although his name has been circulating online over the past 24 hours from some who had received early copies of the game. Regardless, this is our first chance to see the real-life Jason and Lucia together, after years and years of Rockstar secrecy keeping their identities under wraps.

"Thousands of hours, countless memories, and one HELL of a ride!" Lee continued. "The amount of blood, sweat, tears, and IMPACT that went into bringing this world to life is unreal! Oh, and did I mention the impact?!... Yeah, that s***'s REAL!!! 😂💥😵‍💫

"So many incredibly talented people poured their hearts and souls into this game, and I'm beyond grateful to have been part of something so massive! A special shoutout to Manni and Dylan! ❤️ You two are truly amazing humans, inside and out! So much talent, heart, and genuine goodness. I'm forever grateful to have shared this wild ride with you both! Thank you for being so freaking awesome! ❤️❤️❤️

"To everyone who helped make this game possible, thank you for an unforgettable experience! ❤️ And to everyone about to experience Vice City… **BUCKLE UP, BITCHESSSSS!!!!!!!** 😈🔥 **WELCOME TO VICE CITY!!!**"

Like Perez, Rourke is an actor with a history of TV guest roles in series you'll have heard of, including Modern Family and Grey's Anatomy — though no real breakout appearances to date. Of course, all of that has now changed with the actor fronting one of the biggest entertainment releases of all time.

Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Pistols - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Nothing beats the classic side piece. There are 8 different types of Pistols in GTA 6, each with its own speciality in damage, accuracy, range, and handling.
articles.body:
Nothing beats the classic side piece. There are 8 different types of Pistols in GTA 6, each with its own speciality in damage, accuracy, range, and handling. In this official IGN GTA 6 guide , you'll find a detailed overview of the available pistols that you can purchase and unlock so you can complete your arsenal. There are also Unique Weapon Variants for some Pistols.

Here is the list of Standard Pistols you can find in GTA 6:

Here is the list of Variant Pistols you can find in GTA 6:

The Scorpio Nipper .38 is a Compact Pistol with a black finish and a textured grip featuring branding near the top and base.

The Girardi ES9 is a Military Pistol with a sleek black finish and a textured grip featuring a logo near the middle.

The Girardi ES18 is a Burst Pistol with a sleek black finish and a textured grip featuring a logo near the middle. It closely resembles the Girardi ES9 with some added modifications.

The Klose K17 is a Service Pistol with a matte black finish and a lightly textured grip featuring some minor branding near the base.

The Klose K17 MCD is an Automatic Pistol with a matte black finish and a lightly textured grip featuring some minor branding near the base. It closely resembles the Klose K17 with some added modifications.

The Schlamm DRX is a Tactical Pistol with a matte black finish, a lightly textured grip, and minor branding on the slide.

The Duke 1992 is a Heavy Pistol with a matte black finish and brown textured grip panels.

The Fairview Kalinga .50 is a .50 Cal Pistol with a matte black finish and a lightly textured grip featuring a logo near the middle.

There are 30 Unique Variant Pistols in GTA 6 in total. The list below includes images of each Unique Variant Pistol, weapon stats, and info on how to collect them:

The Assassin Nipper .38 Unique Weapon Variant is a Compact Pistol found on the southeastern edge of Permit Keys, east of the Mile Zero Air Station.

You can find the Unique Variant pistol hidden in a small hatch in the floor of a shipwrecked boat. The Assassin Nipper .38 is tied to a side activity puzzle involving a "spy boat".

The Low Point Nipper .38 Unique Weapon Variant is a Compact Pistol, a variant of the Nipper .38 pistol with a rough exterior appearance.

The Turnt Nipper .38 Unique Weapon Variant is a Compact Pistol, a colorful variant of the Nipper .38 which can only be found in a crashed paraglider strung from a tree in Bobcat Bight.

Look for the Turnt Nipper .38 in the seat of the "paratrike" stuck up in the tree. You can find this strange crash site on the northern tip of Bobcat Bay, west of North Mariana County.

The Zodiac Nipper .38 is a Compact Pistol with a blue and purple aesthetic which can be looted during the Ocean Beach Lab Illegal Operation, located in Ocean City.

The Duval Signature ES9 is a Military Pistol, a variant of the ES9 with a sleek, if plain, appearance. It can only be obtained if you own the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition.

Quarter Mile ES9 is a Military Pistol with a sleek silver frame and wooden grip, which can be looted from the Chatfield Storage & Logistics Illegal Operation located in Waxman Island, east of Downtown Vice City.

The Sand Storm ES9 is a Military Pistol with a light gray color and an American flag emboss on the grip. It can be purchased from Big Shots Ammu-Nation store for $1,470. You can find Big Shots on the east side of Hamlet.

The Guardian ES18 is a Burst Pistol with a cream white grip and gold accents. It can be looted during the Saber Shipping Yard Illegal Operation located in Little Cuba, a neighborhood of Vice City.

The Caminos Signature K17 is a Service Pistol with a dark red grip and an opacalescent rose detailing.

DWNPLY's K17 is a Service Pistol with a bright white color and yellow-gold accents.

PTT Youngin$ K17 is a colorful Service Pistol with street art graffiti details, featuring splashes of blue, yellow, and orange. It can be looted during the Kamar Devon Community Center Illegal Operation located in Southside, a neighborhood just north of South Vice-Dale County.

The San4San K17 is a Service Pistol with a modern aesthetic, touched with gold accents, including a scope. It can be looted during the Sound4Sound Studio Illegal Operation found in Stockyard, located on the northernmost end of Vice City.

The Nite Raptor K17 is Service Pistol with a light gray camo aesthetic. It can be purchased at Black Eagle for $2,050. You can find Black Eagle Ammu-Nation weapons store in Balsero, a neighborhood west of Vice City and just east of Bucksin Swamp.

The Dumpster K17 MCD is an Automatic Pistol with a dark purple frame and a "Grease Nation" decal on its grip.

The Stoner K17 MCD is an Automatic Pistol with a sleek black-and-white aesthetic.

At the Big Day Motel off of US-35 just north of Ambrosia, inside room 115. Don't mind the people inside the room. Simply enter to find the Stoner K17 MCD on the nightstand to the right of the bed.

The Patriarch DRX is a Tactical Pistol with a matte black frame and accents of metallic purple-blue.

In a submerged car in the southwest part of the Kalaga Reservoir. Look for luggage and miscellaneous items strewn about near the bank, then head into the water to find the sunken car just past the overgrown algae. Pick up the Patriarch DRX beside the car underwater.

The Rogue Alpha DRX is a Tactical Pistol with a sleek light-gray aesthetic and a dark gray "star" detail on the barrel. It can be purchased at Quickscope for $4,410. You can find the Quickscope Ammu-Nation store across the street from Kensinger Tower in Downtown Vice City.

The Brainwasher 1992 is a Heavy Pistol with a pink and white psychedelic detail on the frame and green and white checkered pattern on its grip.

Brian's 1992 is a Heavy Pistol with a sleek black frame and dark wooden grip.

The Deadringer 1992 is a Heavy Pistol with a silver frame and light wooden grip, both embossed with filigree details.

You can find the Deadringer 1992 inside a mobile home on the south bank of the Moreau River in East Lummox County. Don't be alarmed by the man who may run at you. Head inside and look on the floor to find it by a man's feet.

The Money Bag 1992 is a Heavy Pistol with a dark steel frame and wooden grip, with filigree embossed into the barrel.

Inside a mobile home on the south bank of the Moreau River in East Lummox County. Don't be alarmed by the man who may run at you. Head inside and look on the couch to the right to find the Money Bag 1922.

Martha's 1992 is a Heavy Pistol with a rusted metal frame and worn wooden grip, with "M&L" carved into the grip.

In the fireplace of an old, abandoned "Outlaw's Cabin" in Moreau. Enter the cellar of the structure by going down the stairs on its southeast side. Climb the stairs straight up into the main room, then search the fireplace to find Martha's 1922.

Monty's 1992 is a Heavy Pistol with a yellow-gold coloring, embossed frame, and a filigree texture inlaid in the grip.

Raul's 1992 is a Heavy Pistol with a sleek steel gray frame and black grip, with the decal "CAPO" on the barrel's side.

Russo's 1992 is a Heavy Pistol with a steel frame with a greenish sheen, and a dark wooden grip.

The Silver 1992 is a Heavy Pistol with a shiny steel frame and textured grip, with the decal "CAPO" on the barrel's side. It can be purchased at Big Shots for $2,210. You can find Big Shots Ammu-Nation weapon store on the east side of Hamlet, a neighborhood south of Vice City.

The Black Eagle Import Kalinga is a .50 Cal Pistol with a dark gray frame and bright red grip. Its barrel has zebra accents embossed along the top.

You can find the Black Eagle Import Kalinga inside the Black Eagle warehouse besides the Black Eagle store in Balsero. The Black Eagle Import Kalinga .50 is inside the safe in the office in the front corner. Find the code to the safe by looking at the log in screen of the desktop inside the office. The office is also protected by a keycode.

The Convict Kalinga .50 is a .50 Cal Pistol with a dark purple frame and grip, featuring accents of black and bright red.

Gil's Kalinga .50 is a .50 Pistol with a spray-painted red and black frame, and a... questionable placement of a woman illustrated along the grip.

articles.body:
There are 5 different types of Revolvers in GTA 6, each with its own speciality in damage, accuracy, range, and handling. In this official IGN GTA 6 guide , you'll find a detailed overview of the available Revolvers that you can purchase and unlock so you can complete your arsenal.

We're still tracking down some Assault Rifles, but in the meantime, feel free to use this sortable table for your weapon shopping needs.

Here is a list of all the Standard Revolvers we have found in GTA 6:

Here is a list of all the Variant Revolvers we have found in GTA 6:

The Iron & Oak WCR-1 is a Compact Revolver with an orange frame and golden wooden grip. It can be purchased at Iron & Oak for $1,260. You can find Iron & Oak in the northernmost end of Vice City, in a neighborhood called Stockyard.

The Cargo H&L .38 is a Double Action Revolver with a gray frame and brown wooden grip, with burnished-blue metal accents.

In a yellow "Scoop" shipping container in the cargo area of Port Vice City. Behind the stack of containers it's in, there's another stack, with one container short enough to climb. Use it to climb to the top of this stack, then jump to the rust container.

Climb over the black container to reach the yellow shipping container on the other side. Break into the yellow shipping container to find the Cargo H&L .38. Be wary of security here.

Donnie's H&L .38 is a Double Action Revolver with a black frame and light gray grip, embossed withy details of a hawk and flowers.

Lyle's H&L .38 is a Double Action Revolver with a rusted frame and worn wooden grip. It has the detail "M&L" engraved in the barrel.

You will find Lyle's H&L .38 in the trunk of a car inside an old barn at the deadend of a road in Bonanza. Enter from the side door, then open the trunk to find Lyle's H&L .38.

Ride Free H&L .38 is a Double Action Revolver with a narrow wooden grip, and shiny dark gray barrel. It has the Hawk & Little local engraved on the side. It can be looted during the Biker Hideout Illegal Operation located in Leonard County. You can find the Biker Hideout in a small building on the southern shore of Lake Leonida, west along the road heading out of Ambrosia.

The Jack Sheepe H&L .38 is a Double Action Revolver with a cherry red frame and textured grip. It has a "Jack Sheepe" decal along its narrow barrel. The Jack Sheepe H&L .38 is only available if you have purchased the Ultimate Edition of GTA 6. You can purchase the Jack Sheepe H&L .38 at Biff's Gun Supply for $2,260. You can find Biff's Gun Supply in the northwestern corner of Ambrosia, the town southwest of Lake Leonida.

The Couch Potato Mustang .357 is a Magnum Revolver with a rusted black aesthetic, and white grip tape tied around the grip. You can find th Couch Potato Mustang .357 hidden inside a couch hanging from a tree in front of a mobile home off of Tanglewood Ln. in Port Gellhorn.

Shoot the ropes attached to the couch to release it to the ground. Then, sit on the couch to find the Couch Potato Mustang .357

The Honky Tonk Mustang .357 is a Magnum Revolver with a vintage aesthetic, sporting a dark brown barrel and grip with burnished gold accents. It can be purchased at Phil's Ammu-Nation for $3,780. You can find Phil's Ammu-Nation on the soutmost side of Vice City, in a neighborhood called Southside.

The Kingfishers Akulus is a Heavy Revolver with a camo aesthetic and black grip. It can be looted during the Sunrise RV Park Illegal Operation . You can find the Sunrise RV Park north of Cottonmouth Lake, northwest of Key Lento and Gambit Bay.

The Swamp Bait Akulus is a Heavy Revolver with a gray steel barrel and warped green-and-black grip.

You can find the Swamp Bait Akulus in the marsh just south west of Hamlet inside a waterfront structure. The Swamp Bait Akulus is on the floor inside the larger structure.

articles.body:
There are 11 different Shotguns in GTA 6, each with its own speciality in damage, accuracy, range, and handling. There are also Unique Weapon Variants for some Shotguns.

In this official IGN GTA 6 guide , you'll find a detailed overview of the available Shotguns that you can purchase and unlock to complete your arsenal.

We're still tracking down some Shotguns, but in the meantime, feel free to use this sortable table for your weapon shopping needs.

Here is a list of Standard Shotguns you can find in GTA 6:

Here is a list of all the Variant Shotguns we have found in GTA 6:

The Gutterball Moreland 850 is a Pump Action Shotgun with a blue and black ombre color, and a bowling pin decal on its stock. It can be looted during the Kingpin Bowling Illegal Operation located in Port Gellhorn. You can find the abandoned Kingpin Bowling alley on the south end of Gellhorn.

The Watcher Pro Moreland 850 is a Pump Action Shotgun with an olive green frame, black stock, and black grip. It can be purchased from Tactical Outlet Guns for $1,470. You can find Tactical Outlet Guns Ammu-Nation store on the far west side of Belville.

The CPD Moreland 850 is a Pump Action Shotgun with a light silver frame and black stock and grip.

San4San Gorse 425 is a Stubby Shotgun with a dull gold frame, and San4San Gorse accents decorated along its grip and stock. It can be looted during the Parlor Apartments Illegal Operation located in Rockridge. You can find the Parlor Apartments across the street from the Rockridge Blood Center in the southwest corner of the neighborhood.

Smuggler Gorse 425 is a Stubby Shotgun with a dull green frame, and a spray painted decal of a death's head moth near the stock.

It can be found in an abandoned smuggler's boat washed up on the shore of a small island east of Mile Zero Air Station, in Permit Keys.

The Basher Gorse 425 is a Stubby Shotgun with a dull tan frame and worn brown stock. It can be purchased at the Pawn & Gun located in Port Gellhorn. You can find this location of the Pawn & Gun Ammu-Nation store towards the south side of Gellhorn.

The Dirty Drifter is a Double Barrel Shotgun with a black barrel, gold accents, and a stock decorated with gray-green and brown brush strokes.

You can find the Dirty Drifte in the trunk of a blue car stuck in a mudslide, just off the coastal road in Bonanza. Climb the bank where the mudslide happened and open the trunk of the car to find the Dirty Drifter.

The Darknite Drifter is a Double Barrel Shotgun with gold filigree embossed on its barrel, and an old-timey illustration on its stock. It can be purchased at the Shrewsbury Drifter for $2,420. You can find the Shrewsbury Drifter Ammu-Nation store along the northwest edge of Port Gellhorn/

The Marabunta Grande Hobo is a Double Barrel Sawed-Off Shotgun with dark wooden accents on its barrel and stock, and gold filigree inlaid above its trigger, including the words "La Familia Primero".

The Backdoor Hobo is a Double Barrel Sawed-Off Shotgun with yellow tape wrapped around its brown wooden stock. It can be purchased at Zenon's Pawn Shop for $2,502. You can find Zenon's Pawn Shop Ammu-Nation store in La Perle, a neighborhood in north Vice City.

The Final Chapter Shortstraw is a Sporting Sawed-Off with a chestnut wooden grip and stock, and two ducks embossed near the trigger. It can be looted during the Hog Stars Garage Illegal Operation, located in Ambrosia. You can find Hog Stars Garage nearby the Pay 'N' Spray in Ambrosia.

The Woodhatch Longshot is a Sporting Shotgun with a sleek wooden stock and black barrel. It can be purchased at Woodhatch for $2,990. You can find the Woodhatch Ammu-Nation store in Capri, the wealthy neighborhood west of North Mariana County.

The Nitepower AZ1200 is a Semi-Auto Shotgun with a gray camo wrap job and an eagle decal on its stock. It can be purchased at Black Eagle for $4,830. You can find the Black Eagle Ammu-Nation store right by the Griffin Shooting Range, on the north side of Balsero.

The Throttler Vero is a Semi-Auto Stubby Shotgun with a yellow and red flame decal along its frame. It can be looted during the Farm Fix Meth Lab Illegal Operation, located in the northern half of Belville, south of Lake Leonida.

The Hostile Super400 is a Heavy Shotgun with a light blue frame and graffiti art-style accents on its frame and stock. It can be looted during the Mill Station Radar Base Illegal Operation, located in Grassrivers. You can find Mill Station Radar Base north of Watson Bay.

The Bruiser Super400 is a Heavy Shotgun with a dark wooden stock and grip, and dull black barrel. It can be purchased at Vice City Gun & Pawn for $5,930. You can find Vice City Gun & Pawn on the south side of Rockridge in Vice City.

The Final Chapter KVGA-12 is an Auto Shotgun with a faded wooden frame and black stock. It has flames and grim reaper decals embossed on it. It can be looted during the Irons Building Supply Illegal Operation located in Ambrosia, the town southwest of Lake Leonida.

Hellspawn Comshot 12 is a Combat Shotgun with a dark red frame and an uncomfortably... fleshy looking grip.

The Hellspawn Comshot is the reward for completing a challenge located at a campsite off a side road in the mountains in the west of North Kelly County.

The challenge is triggered by eating something on the carved wooden throne here. Survive and complete the challenge to find the Hellspawn Comshot 12 leaning against the throne. You'll get a new Circles of Hell shirt, too.

The Unpacked Comshot 12 is a Combat Shotgun with a dull black, minimalist aesthetic.

The Unpacked Comshot 12 is in an ensuite upstairs bathroom behind the door in a house on the northwest coast of Key Lento. Head up the outdoor stairs and break into the second story. From either door, make a right down the hallway and turn left into a back bedroom, and look for an ensuite bathroom on the left. Enter the bathroom.

The Unpacked Comshot 12 is behind the bathroom door, leaning against the wall. There's actually a note on the kitchen counter about the unpacked gun, too, alerting you to its existence in the first place.

articles.title: Sniper Rifles - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: There are at least 18 different Sniper Rifles in GTA 6, each with its own speciality in damage, accuracy, range, and handling. There are also Unique Weapon
articles.body:
There are at least 18 different Sniper Rifles in GTA 6, each with its own speciality in damage, accuracy, range, and handling. There are also Unique Weapon Variants for some Sniper Rifles.

In this official IGN GTA 6 guide , you'll find a detailed overview of the available Sniper Rifles that you can purchase and unlock to complete your arsenal.

We're still tracking down some Sniper Rifles, but in the meantime, feel free to use this sortable table for your weapon shopping needs.

Here is a list of Standard Sniper Rifles you can find in GTA 6:

Here is a list of all the Variant Sniper Rifles we have found in GTA 6:

The Hunter's Laird 350 is a Sporting Sniper Rifle with a beautifully warped wooden frame, featuring stripes of brown, blue, and gray.

Kingfishers Laird 350 is a Sporting Sniper Rifle with a unique gray camo wrap job, featuring hints of white, black, and orange. You can loot the Kingfishers Laird 350 during the Manatee Motel Illegal Operation located in Gullet Marsh, just a bit southwest of Hamlet.

The Mister Mangrove Laird 350 is a Sporting Sniper Rifle with a green camo wrap around its frame and stock.

Twin's Laird 350 is a Sporting Sniper Rifle with a dark wood frame and sleek black barrel.

You can find the Twin's Laird 350 below a small hunting platform in the woods just east of Kalaga Reservoir in Lummox County. Look for the scene of an unfortunate accident involving a hunter to find the Twin's Laird 350 on the ground nearby.

The Cruel Huntsman's SM-69 is a Hunting Sniper Rifle with a beautiful warped wood body, featuring stripes of blue-gray and brown.

You can find the Cruel Huntsman's SM-69 on the boardwalk of a hunter's cabin in the Pelican Valley marsh in Marion County. The Cruel Huntsman's SM-69 is on the floor between the two buildings, by some gator carcasses.

The Fincredible Laird 350 is a Sporting Sniper Rifle with a green fish scale wrap around its frame, making the stock appear like an open-mouthed fish. It can be purchased at Guns Aplenty! for $2000. Look for Guns Aplenty! in Watson Bay, a small neighborhood west of Hamlet and the Gullet Marsh.

The Killtelligence SM-69 is a Hunting Sniper Rifle with a gray camo frame and sleek black barrel. Killtelligence SM-69 is given you to by Bret Vogel when starting the Hunting side quests .

The Firebreak SM-69 is a Hunting Sniper Rifle with an orange and gray-style camo wrap. It can be purchased at R. Willis Jr. Supplies for $3,890. You can find the R. Willis Jr. Supplies Ammu-Nation store in Lummox County, northwest of Kalaga Reservoir.

The Gun Nut SMS-01 is an Advanced Sniper Rifle with an American flag wrap with flames and "America" written across the frame.

The IAA SMS-01 is an Advanced Sniper Rifle with a long black frame and barrel, and an army green scope.

You can find the IAA SMS-01 on the very top of the roof of Aichi Condominiums on Northside Ave on Washington Beach.

You must complete a related Mission in order for this Unique Weapon Variant to appear at this location.

The FIB SM-69 is a Hunting Sniper Rifle with a matte black frame.

You can find the FIB SM-69 at the top of a skyscraper in Vice Beach, between two hospitals.

You need to complete a related mission before the FIB SM-69 will appear in this location.

The Internal Affairs FF-SR is a Combat Sniper Rifle with a dull green frame and black accents.

You can find the Internal Affairs FF-SR at the top of a skyscraper on Washington Beach, where there's a helicopter pad. The northwest edge of the roof of the tallest building on this stretch of Northside Ave.

The Island Poacher FF-50 is a Heavy Sniper Rifle with a dull green cam wrap with a decal of a three-headed dog, surrounded by a circle with the words "Sapienter Si Sincere".

articles.title: Submachine Guns - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: There are at least 32 different Submachine Guns in GTA 6, each with its own speciality in damage, accuracy, range, and handling. There are also Unique Weapon
articles.body:
There are at least 32 different Submachine Guns in GTA 6, each with its own speciality in damage, accuracy, range, and handling. There are also Unique Weapon Variants for some Submachine Guns.

In this official IGN GTA 6 guide , you'll find a detailed overview of the available Submachine Guns that you can purchase and unlock to complete your arsenal.

Here is a list of Submachine Guns you can find in GTA 6:

Here is a list of all the Variant Submachine Guns we have found in GTA 6:

Bae-Lux's W-10 is a Micro SMG, with an ombre purple-and-pink wrap job, accented with zebra stripes.

The Chromium W-10 is a Micro SMG with a chrome, cylindrical barrel. It can be looted during the La Perle Trap House Illegal Operation located on the north side of Vice City. You can find the La Perle Trap House in a neighborhood called La Perle.

The Little Friend W-10 is a Micro SMG with a matte black-gray finish.

You can find the Little Friend W-10 in a room on the second floor of the Sunlite Motel in Ocean Beach off of Shore Drive. Go up the stairs beneath the red awning to find a doorway splattered with blood on the right. The Little Friend W-10 is just inside on the floor amongst a crime scene.

Roxy's W-10 is a cute Micro SMG with a magenta wrap job, featuring cheetah print accents.

Tyrone's W-10 is a Micro SMG with a dull gold frame and grip.

The Moneymaker W-10 is a Micro SMG with a navy blue frame and gold accents, including a shiny gold barrel. It can be purchased at Tequesta Guns & Ammo for $1,557. Look for Tequesta Guns & Ammo in the southwest part of Tequesta.

The Marabunta Grande Type 9 is a Machine Pistol SMG, with gold accents along its barrel, frame, and magazine. It can be looted during the Weed Grow Illegal Operation, located in East Lummox County. You can find the Weed Grow farm on the northeast shore of Lake Tallaloko.

The Neon Sunset Type 9 is a Machine Pistol SMG with a navy blue frame, neon blue barrel, and pink graffiti art-style decals. It can be purchased at Vice City Firearms for $2,310. You can find Vice City Firearms in Salton.

In an underground armory beneath a hatch in a mobile home in Balsero, just south west of the Griffin Shooting Range.

Enter the mobile home through a side door, open the latch in the back, and climb down the ladder to find the Conspiracist Type 9 on the table.

The Eris Fresh DSG is a Tactical SMG which can be looted during the Illegal Goods Store Illegal Operation. You can find the Illegal Goods Store on the northern end of Southside, one of the southmost neighborhoods of Vice City.

The Chronic Vatra is a Heavy SMG with neon green and purple accents, and a decal of two skeletal hands reaching out along the stock. It can be looted during the Industrial Weed Grow Illegal Operation , located in North Mariana County. You can find the Industrial Weed Grow headquartered north of Tola Bay and Big Pine.

The Double Cross Vatra is a Heavy SMG with a severely rusted frame.

articles.title: Fallout-Themed AriZona Iced Tea Gets Black Friday Discount, Including New 'Apocalyptic Orange' Flavor
articles.body:
Amazon’s Black Friday sale is officially live , making it a great time to pick up some serious bulk of whatever your drink of choice is. Mine happens to be AriZona Iced Tea, because who can hate cheap caffeine, and I’ll certainly never complain about a deal dropping those prices even further.

The 15oz Fallout edition teas only come in 12-can packs, priced at around $2/can. Don’t worry, AriZona still maintains its 99-cent MSRP for non-licensed drinks — founder Don Vultaggio makes sure of that. The Amazon discount only knocks off a couple of bucks, but it brings every Fallout can closer to that beautiful standard price.

Amazon Discounts Fallout AriZona Green Tea Packs for Black Friday

AriZona x Fallout Energy Drink - Green Tea Variety Pack, 15 fl oz (12 Pack)

AriZona x Fallout Energy Drink - Pomegranate Green Tea - 15 fl oz (12 Pack)

AriZona x Fallout Energy Drink - Red Apple Green Tea - 15 fl oz (12 Pack)

AriZona x Fallout Energy Drink - Sweet Peach Green Tea - 15 fl oz (12 Pack)

AriZona x Fallout Energy Drink - Orange Green Tea - 15 fl oz (12 Pack)

The 15% discount is available on 12-can cases of individual flavors as well as the bulk variety pack. All packs have the same base price, so the decision really comes down to your flavor preferences.

Your Fallout options consist of three Vault-Tec reimaginings of AriZona classics – Atomic Red Apple, Wastelander Sweet Peach, and Power Pomegranate – and Apocalyptic Orange, a new flavor unique to the collaboration.

The flavors are tied to specific characters from Amazon’s live-action series, depicted in playing card illustrations on the packaging of each case. Lucy gets apple and the Ghoul gets peach, while Dogmeat and pre-war Ghoul adorn the low-cal versions.

The collaboration also doubled up on Maximus drinks, with orange dedicated to the man and pomegranate dedicated to his Power Armor. I guess it could be someone else in the suit, but I leave that up to your interpretation.

Fallout TV Show Video Game Easter Eggs – Vault-Tec / Iconography

Amazon’s Fallout TV show has brought a whole new audience to Bethesda’s post-apocalyptic world . The series aired its second season earlier this year, and a third season should be coming to Prime Video at some point in 2027.

Bethesda, on the other hand, has turned its attention back to the world of Elder Scrolls. The company announced Sentinel as the name of the next game, though it likely won’t arrive for several more years . Bethesda confirmed Fallout 5 won’t be coming until after the next Elder Scrolls, so it might be quite the wait until we get a new journey in the Wasteland.

articles.title: Percy Jackson Actors Reveal They Watched Attack on Titan Fan Edits to Help Themselves Cry While Filming Emotional Scenes
articles.summary: Walker Scobell and Aryan Simhadri revealed that they would watch Attack on Titan fan edits to help them prepare to film emotional scenes for Percy Jackson and the Olympians.
articles.body:
Walker Scobell and Aryan Simhadri revealed that they would watch Attack on Titan fan edits to help them prepare to film emotional scenes for Percy Jackson and the Olympians.

Attack on Titan is one of the most popular anime series in the world, in no small part due to its tragic storylines and brutal, gory battles. It’s been more than a decade since the anime first released in 2013, and fans have been making AMVs of their favorite characters ever since — but these fans probably didn’t know that their creations would help high-profile actors tap into their emotions.

Speaking at 92NY on a live episode of Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast, Walker Scobell revealed his unique method for getting himself into an emotional state in preparation for sad scenes while filming Percy Jackson and the Olympians .

Percy Jackson Season 1: Episodes 1-8 Gallery

Scobell said that he would watch fan-made edits for Eren and Mikasa, two of Attack on Titan’s main characters, set to the opening song of Season 3, Red Swan.

“I was trying to get sad. I was in school, and I snuck my phone in. I was like, ‘What can I do to make myself cry?’ I searched up a bunch of — and he did the exact same thing, and we just figured this out yesterday,” Scobell said, pointing to co-star Aryan Simhadri.

“We didn’t communicate this at all. We just ended up doing it,” Simhardi confirmed.

“I thought of the saddest thing I could, and I searched up Eren and Mikasa edits from Attack on Titan,” Scobell continued. “I started crying at school, watching them to Red Swan. And then I got there [on set], and I couldn’t do it.”

Walker & Aryan saying they watch eren & mikasa edits so they can cry on set is actually frying meee 😭😭😭 — ELON SMD (@pearlinasbeau) November 20, 2026

Walker & Aryan saying they watch eren & mikasa edits so they can cry on set is actually frying meee 😭😭😭

Fans in the crowd had excited reactions to this revelation, as did fans online when clips from the episode made their way on social media shortly thereafter.

“Their tragedy is so profounddd everyone can feel it… oh they really are modern day Romeo and Juliet,” one fan wrote on X/Twitter.

“Red Swan is a Top 3 OP, I don’t blame him,” another said.

“The way they're emotionally regulating through anime edits on a professional set is the most Gen Z actor thing I've ever heard,” another remarked.

It’s no wonder that actors take notes from Attack on Titan for their own projects; in fact, Eren’s English voice actor, Bryce Papenbrook, revealed that he literally unhinged his jaw while screaming in one of the anime’s most iconic scenes in an effort to really sell the character’s pain and confusion.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3, The Titan’s Curse , is streaming on Disney+ and Hulu right now with new episodes dropping every Friday through December 11, 2026.

articles.title: The Official Lord of the Rings Pizza Cutter Drops to a New Low Price at Amazon
articles.body:
Amazon's Black Friday sale is a great time to find discounts on things you actually need. It's also a great time to buy expensive gifts for yourself that you absolutely don't need. Somewhere in between those two extremes is where I like to do most of my online window shopping, which is what led me to this discount on the official Lord of the Rings Pizza Wheel.

Amazon is currently offering a 20% discount, which drops the price down to $159.99 for the first time ever. It's a very expensive pizza cutter for sure, but it's also one of the coolest LOTR gifts for your kitchen you'll find anywhere.

Dalstrong Pizza Wheel - Lord of the Rings

As someone who makes a lot of pizzas at home, I can attest to how important it is to have a good pizza cutter at your disposal. If you don't have a sharp enough blade, toppings get crushed and pepperonis do that thing where they disappear into the cracks of every cut. You're only going to get good pizza slices if you have a knife capable of cutting good slices.

Dalstrong, the brand who makes this product, uses high-quality German X50CrMoV15 steel for their knives and pizza cutters. This gives them solid toughness and corrosion resistance that will help keep the blade sharper for longer. This type of steel isn't going to hold an edge nearly as long as the high-end Japanese variety, but it's fairly easy to sharpen and hone at home if the edge does get dull. Just don't go putting it in the dishwasher!

As for the LOTR stuff that actually makes this pizza cutter cool, there's a lot to love in the design. The handle is made of ebony wood and copper accents with the Leaf of Lórien carved into it. The blade itself is left bare to ensure drag-free cutting, but both sides include different designs etched into the steel. On one side you get silhouettes of the members of The Fellowship of the Ring and on the other side you get an inscription written in Elvish. I can't actually read Elvish, but I hope it just says pizza multiple times.

The pizza wheel also comes with a collector's pin and a leather sheath to help protect the blade. The whole thing ships in the kind of premium gift packaging that you'd expect from a nearly $200 pizza cutter.

The 4K Movie Trilogy Is Also on Sale Today

The Lord of the Rings: The Motion Picture Trilogy

Amazon also has a great deal on the 4K collection going on right now that's worth checking out. This includes both the theatrical and extended editions of the film in full 4K UHD. If you're only streaming these movies with an HBO Max subscription, you're missing out on the full visual experience.

A Test of Skill is an early game quest given to you by the Hunter. To trigger it, you must reach level 7, complete the main quest Hunter Becomes the Hunted , and speak to the Hunter to receive the quest. A Test of Skill involves finding an ancient obelisk in the Revelwood region.

To get there, fast travel to the Revelwood Ancient Spire. The obelisk is rather close to the tower, but the easiest way to get there is through Thornhold, which is just southeast of the Ancient Spire.

Once at the tower, leap off the southeastern side of the tower and soar as far as you can, keeping an eye on the road below. If you managed to fly in a somewhat straight line, you would have been able to land on the road.

Follow the road southeast until you come across a fork. Take the path leading right, then take the smaller path leading left. Follow that to the end to reach Thornhold, but avoid running straight in. There are a lot of Scavengers in this camp, and they wield some pretty powerful cannon weapons that can easily wipe you out if you're not careful.

One is positioned on a high lookout tower inside the gate on the right, which is quite hard to reach. Climbing the ladder results in getting shot down, so try to pick him off with long-range projectiles if you can.

Follow the main road through the stronghold, defeating Scavengers as you go, and approach the exit on the western side of the settlement.

It's boarded up with wooden planks, so destroy them with an axe and jump over the barricade to find another road. Follow that road all the way to the end to reach the obelisk, and interact with it to complete A Test of Skill !

articles.title: How a $6 Beer in GTA 6 Sent Me Into a Spiral of Crime and Anxiety
articles.body:
I'm relationship-maxxing GTA 6. Forget the money, the cars, or building a criminal empire. My main aim is to make Jason and Lucia so disgustingly loved up that NPCs violently vomit as we walk past being all cute together. I want them to be the perfect couple. I want romance. I want devotion. I want the sort of relationship that makes everyone else in Vice City feel deeply inadequate.

Unfortunately, the nuanced way GTA 6 tracks even the smallest actions has turned me into a paranoid lunatic, constantly worrying that one wrong move will destroy my carefully cultivated romance. Case in point: a $6 beer that sent me into a cascade of disasters, petty crime, and emotional turmoil, eventually ending with me restarting an entire mission because I was worried I'd blown it.

Early on in the game, you're given the chance to prepare the house and complete some simple objectives ahead of picking Lucia up from prison. Naturally, I did them all. Fixed the steps, bought the necklace, got the flowers. I even made sure the car was dent-free, had a haircut and a shower, and dressed my Jason in his best jeans and shirt. My man was going to look presentable when he picked up the love of his life. I was on my best behavior. Nothing was going to stop me getting to my girl.

In fact, I was so determined to be the perfect boyfriend that I even avoided committing any crimes on the way to the prison. In Grand Theft Auto. I obeyed traffic laws. I stopped at red lights. I avoided trouble wherever possible, to the point that when a random NPC tried to mug me, I just handed over my cash rather than risk getting into a fight. Remember that last part. It's important.

After picking Lucia up from prison, you head straight to the Rusty Anchor for a few drinks. So far, so good. We've got the flowers, the necklace, the freshly showered boyfriend. This is going brilliantly. Then Lucia wanders off for a moment and asks Jason to get her a drink.

Shit. I have no money. Suddenly, my decision to be a law-abiding citizen has come back to bite me in the arse. I gave all my money to a mugger because I was trying to be a good boyfriend, and now I can't afford to buy my girlfriend a beer. A beer that costs just $6.

Surely this is a relationship test? If I follow Lucia without her drink, am I getting a little broken heart icon? Is this going into some invisible ledger of romantic failures? Have I already failed as a boyfriend, future husband, and potential co-parent because I can't produce one lousy alcoholic beverage?

I start looking for solutions. I check every bottle in the bar, hoping I can just grab one and pretend I've paid for it. They're all empty. I search the entire building for something I could quickly pawn, like a trading card, or even just some random cash someone has carelessly left lying around. Nothing. The panic is setting in.

I head outside and start searching the nearby streets. I don't want a wanted rating, because surely being arrested while Lucia waits patiently for a drink isn't going to do wonders for our relationship either. So I look for cars with trunks I can break into easily. I find a selection of sunglasses and hats, which is lovely, but unless Lucia has suddenly developed a taste for drinking accessories, they're not going to help me.

I'm now seriously considering mugging someone. I only need $6. Six. Dollars. That's barely a crime, right? In the grand scheme of GTA, that's practically community service. I pull out my gun and start advancing on a random NPC walking down the sidewalk. I'm about to threaten an innocent stranger with a deadly weapon so I can buy my girlfriend a beer. This is what love looks like, apparently.

And then it happens. The game suddenly switches to a cutscene of Lucia saying, "You forgot about me?" NO. NO! The opposite! I was thinking about you the entire time! I needed $6 for a beer, light of my life! I was prepared to commit armed robbery for you! Does that mean nothing?

But the damage is done. Or at least, I think the damage is done, which is somehow worse. Has the game registered that I wandered off and abandoned Lucia? Does she think Jason is an inconsiderate arsehole? Have I just knocked several invisible points off my perfect relationship score? Is this going to come back to haunt me 30 hours from now when she remembers that time I left her alone in a bar? I can't take the risk. I restart the checkpoint.

Unfortunately, this creates another problem. The checkpoint puts me right outside the prison, which means I still have no money. I've travelled back in time, but I haven't solved the fundamental issue of being a broke boyfriend.

Luckily, there's a parking lot nearby. This time, I abandon my commitment to good behaviour. I go rogue, breaking open trunks left and right, ignoring alarms and grabbing whatever I can get my hands on. The same man who was carefully obeying traffic laws 20 minutes ago is now systematically robbing parked cars in broad daylight. Eventually, I walk away with $30. A fortune. Five beers' worth of romantic security.

I get Lucia her drink. Crisis averted. Relationship saved. Probably.

And that's the thing about GTA 6 that's completely got its hooks into me. I've become so thoroughly relationship-pilled that I'm making decisions I would never normally consider in a Grand Theft Auto game. I'm not thinking about how much money I can make, how many cars I can steal, or how much chaos I can cause. I'm thinking about whether Jason is being a good boyfriend. I'm worrying about whether Lucia feels appreciated. I'm committing crimes not for personal gain, but in the service of being a thoughtful romantic partner.

It's ridiculous, but it's also fascinating. Rockstar has somehow made me care about the smallest interactions between these two characters to the point where I'm second-guessing everything I do. The possibility that an apparently insignificant action might have consequences for their relationship is enough to make even buying a beer feel like a high-stakes decision.

And the uncertainty is part of what makes it work. I don't know whether failing to buy Lucia that drink would actually have mattered. Maybe she wouldn't have cared. Maybe the game wouldn't have registered it at all. But the fact that I believed it might matter was enough to completely change how I played.

That's a pretty remarkable achievement for a game where I can also steal a sports car and drive it directly into the ocean.

Of course, if I'm already this emotionally compromised over a $6 beer, I dread to think what will happen when Rockstar inevitably throws some huge, emotionally devastating choices at Jason and Lucia later in the narrative. Although, at this point, choosing between love and betrayal might actually be easier than figuring out how to pay for a round of drinks.

Rockstar, you absolute bastards. You've made me into a person who will commit armed robbery rather than disappoint his girlfriend, and somehow you've made it feel romantic. Romance options in games are never going to feel quite the same again.

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

After a series of delays, the Nitro Deck 2 finally launched for the Nintendo Switch 2 this year. Just like its predecessor, it's proving to be one of the Switch 2's hottest accessories for anyone looking to elevate their gaming experience while maintaining comfort over extended periods of time. The Nitro Deck 2 is a step up in essentially every meaningful way, providing a far more premium experience over the original. Some of the most notable are improved ergonomics (including an offset right stick), swappable D-pads and stick tops, a sturdier kickstand, and an updated sliding mechanism for a better fit.

Not only does the Nitro Deck 2 offer considerable improvements over the Switch version, it also sports full backward compatibilty with the Switch and Switch OLED consoles. So you'll have the freedom to swap back and forth between Nintendo's newer and older systems if you ever needed to. It can even be disconnected and used as a pro-style controller for your Switch or Switch 2, PC, or mobile device.

For those who value aesthetics as much as the ydo functionality, the Nitro Deck 2 comes in three standard color variations you can choose from: Smoke Black, Pal Grey, and White. Every variation will run you $79.99 (25% off) while Amazon's sale lasts.

If you want add-ons, you can find them directly from the CRKD website. There are variety of accessories for the Nitro Deck 2, such as a pack of swappable D-pads , an 8-pack of stick tops , and more. There's also the Nitro Deck 2 Hardshell Carry Case for $39.99.

articles.summary: Gathering Wool in the Albaneve Summits is a main quest in Enshrouded that is given to you by the Farmer. If you want to find out exactly how to complete
articles.body:
Gathering Wool in the Albaneve Summits is a main quest in Enshrouded that is given to you by the Farmer . If you want to find out exactly how to complete Gathering Wool in the Albaneve Summits so you can start growing your yak empire, you'll find everything you need in this Enshrouded guide.

Once you reach the Albaneve Summits and ignite the Ancient Spire there, Emily, the Farmer, will have this quest for you next time you talk to her. She also has something else for you, the recipe for Yak Bait. To make the bait you need to tame your future yaks, you'll need the following ingredients:

1x Corncob : Grown from seeds found in Springlands

1x Dried Purple Berry : Purple Berries can be found in the Springlands and dried on the Drying Rack.

Once you've got your Yak Bait, you're ready to set off in search of some yaks to feed it to.

Yaks are found in the Albaneve Summits region and can be tracked down in a few different locations, but the easiest place to go is the entrance to the Quiet Caves in the Wildwater Basin. To get there, fast travel to the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and soar off the northeastern side.

Glide straight forward until you start to approach two windcurrents. Hitch a ride on the currents to the land straight ahead and turn left. Follow that road until you reach the Wildwater Basin. The Quite Caves are along the western side of the Basin, but beware! There is a cyclops waiting for you there.

After dealing with the cyclops, search around the entrance of the cave to find a herd of yak. One you've got your target, crouch down on the ground and start sneaking closer to the yak. Once you get within throwing distance, throw some Yak Food Bait on the ground and wait for the yak to start eating. Once it's distracted, slowly creep forward and pat the yak when you get close enough. Retreat and repeat the process three times to tame the yak!

Once your yak has been successfully tamed, put it in your inventory and bring it back to your base. Craft a paddock big enough for your new critter, and put it in its new enclosure! Now you've got a constant source of wool and a cute new addition to your base.

articles.summary: Cooking Warm Food is a main quest given to you by the Farmer in Enshrouded. You'll get this quest after completing Gathering Wool in the Albaneve Summits,
articles.body:
Cooking Warm Food is a main quest given to you by the Farmer in Enshrouded. You'll get this quest after completing Gathering Wool in the Albaneve Summits , and it sends you on a quick mission to whip up some warming meals in your kitchen.

To complete the Cooking Warm Food quest, you simply have to cook some warm food! There are three recipes you can choose from, and what one is easiest will depend on what ingredients you have on hand. The three meals you can make are as follows:

Pumpkin Soup : 5x Pumpkin, 3x Gentian, 3x Frizzy Goat Milk, 3x Salt

Beef Stew : 2x Eggs, 3x Raw Fatty Meat, 4x Tomato, 3x Frizzy Goat Milk

While the Pumpkin Soup and Beef Stew are both hearty meals that go much further, the Grilled Fatty Beef is, by far, the easiest recipe to make, and the only equipment you need is the Cooking Station. Collect some Raw Fatty Meat by harvesting yak or frizzy goat or by defeating snow leopards. Then, make your way to your Cooking Station and interact with it. Select the meal you want to make and relax until your meal as done. Once your food is fully cooked, the Cooking Warm Food quest will complete!

articles.summary: Give & Gather is an Annual Event that begins on November 19 and will herald the winter season with Hello Kitty Island Adventure as the main event. Join
articles.body:
Give & Gather is an Annual Event that begins on November 19 and will herald the winter season with Hello Kitty Island Adventure as the main event. Join Cinnamoroll in handing out presents to all of your friends throughout Friendship Island. The more you hand out, the more you get in return when it's time to properly celebrate around the Give & Gather tree in Seaside Resort Plaza.

Check in with Friendship Island every day to take part in obtaining Daily Rewards from My Melody in Seaside Resort's plaza area. If you happen to miss her, you can also check your game menu to search for the Daily Rewards tab to claim them that way. Each day promises something new, from exclusive themed outfits and furniture to valuable resources from all around Friendship Island!

Give & Gather's Daily Rewards are broken down into three parts, with Parts I and II lasting 14 days each. Part I will start on the same day as the event, and Part II will begin about a week after the event has started.

Give & Gather is all about celebrating your friends around Friendship Island and reminding them how much you care by handing out presents! Cinnamoroll is busy at work fulfilling orders on the daily in addition to the presents, so he'll need your help in picking a Hello Kitty Character for the day and personally gifting them their character-specific presents. Cinnamoroll will also give you an extra 1x Holiday Gift that you can hand out to anyone on the island. When you give Presents to your friends, whether it's the tasks from Cinnamoroll or the extra gifts he gives you, you'll receive Presents in return. However, these presents will automatically be delivered to the Present Pine Tree in Seaside Resort, next to the Event Stall by the plaza.

Some presents under the Present Pine Tree will be opened once all of the gifts have been delivered, and it is time to come together with all of your friends to celebrate Give & Gather properly! Other presents you can exchange at the Pine Tree early to start unlocking some of the Midwinter-themed furniture for Give & Gather 2026. To get more copies of the Midwinter furniture, you can interact with the small hut next to the Present Pine to exchange Gumdrops . You can also obtain past furniture and outfits from previous Give & Gather events.

Gumdrops are automatically given to you whenever you deliver a present to one of your friends. You'll receive 3x Gumdrops for each present you hand out, and 1x Gumdrop for each Daily Quest you complete, for a total of ~11x Gumdrops per day . If you happen to miss a day, you can make up the missing Gumdrops depending on when you're able to log back in.

Everyone is getting into the holiday spirit this Give & Gather season with outfits to complement the Midwinter theme for 2026. To unlock Hello Kitty Character Outfits, you'll need to participate in the Give & Gather cutscenes that will either automatically play when you log in and talk to My Melody or by checking in with the Master of Festivities.

The Master of Festivities is the Nul that can be found standing behind the Event Stall. Whenever they have a cutscene ready for you to participate in, the Master of Festivities will be waiting just outside the Seaside Resort plaza. Talk to the Nul to select which cutscene event you'd like to watch.

articles.title: 15 años después, los fans de Naruto y el anime por fin podremos disfrutar de KAYOU, el fenómeno que ya ha conquistado China
articles.standfirst: Hemos abierto nuestra primera caja y os enseñamos que nos ha salido.
articles.summary: Hemos abierto nuestra primera caja y os enseñamos que nos ha salido.
articles.body: Durante años, Naruto, One Piece, Dragon Ball y otro buen puñado de series de animación con las que muchos de nosotros crecimos se expandieron por el mundo a través de muy diversos formatos más allá del anime y el manga. De entre todos ellos, hay algunos que siempre han tenido especial relevancia, como los videojuegos... o las cartas. Quienes gustamos de todo este tipo de pasatiempos hemos encontrado en ellas una manera bastante particular de disfrutar de aquello que amamos. Por desgracia, durante años también hemos tenido que sufrir no pocas imitaciones. Al menos así ha sido durante muchos años en Occidente, que no en China. Aunque te pueda resultar extraño, el país asiático fue uno de los pioneros a la hora de producir series de cartas coleccionables con licencias oficiales mediante KAYOU, una empresa que colabora directamente con productoras como Pierrot. Al menos así era hasta ahora, porque en España por fin está disponible. 15 años después de su fundación, KAYOU ha dado el salto a la península a través de Asmodee, poniendo al alcance de nuestras manos estas nuevas series de cartas coleccionables. De momento han llegado Naruto y My Little Pony, pero con el tiempo acabarán llegando más. Como habréis podido imaginar, ha sido esta primera la que más nos ha emocionado. Sobre todo porque esto no es un TCG. KAYOU no viene a competir contra Magic, Lorcana, Pokémon o Yu-Gi-Oh! Es lo que se llama un CCG, puesto que todo se basa en coleccionar. No busca que compitas, sino que colecciones. Pero ¿qué es exactamente KAYOU, por qué se habla tanto de sus cartas y qué las diferencia de otros productos coleccionables? Vamos a descubrirlo. Uno de los aspectos más importantes de KAYOU como CCG es que trabaja con licencias oficiales. Es decir, sus productos son oficiales y se basan en —entre otras cosas— algunos de los animes más famosos del mundo. Por lo tanto, no busca equilibrar potencias ni estilos, sino que lo da todo en ofrecer cartas cuya presentación visual sea muy llamativa. Lo consigue, tanto en sus rarezas mínimas como básicas. Así pues, es puro coleccionismo. Si te gusta, posiblemente sea lo que estás buscando, ya que todas las decisiones de diseño de las distintas franquicias que lo componen se centran en este apartado. Los que lo conocíamos llevábamos mucho tiempo esperándolo. KAYOU como tal nació en 2011 y, desde entonces, Internet se ha encargado de mostrarnos sus colecciones desde la distancia. Adquirirlas en España era o bien una tarea imposible o bien un ejercicio de confianza económica en el que no podías recurrir a tiendas especialmente confiables. Solo podíamos disfrutarlas desde la distancia. O al menos así era hasta ahora, porque por fin contamos con distribución oficial. Y no es que empezasen con Naruto, pero sí que empezaron su actividad hace 15 años. Muchos lo descubrieron casi al principio, así que también eran muchos los que llevan más de una década pidiendo su llegada. El primer acercamiento ha sido mediante Naruto y, más concretamente, con su serie 01. Dedicada al universo de Masashi Kishimoto, reúne a los principales protagonistas de la serie con un estilo claramente marcado por el anime. Destaca en lo artístico, con ilustraciones y acabados muy notables y con una paleta de colores muy viva. Con rarezas bien diferenciadas y especialmente enfocadas al coleccionismo, parte con una base de 158 cartas. Hay un total de diez rarezas diferentes y esta primera edición se inspira en los pergaminos y se basa en las primeras sagas del anime. Cada caja contiene 20 sobres. Sobre si merece o no la pena, como siempre, todo depende de tus gustos. A mí, por ejemplo, me encanta Naruto. Es una de las series de animación con las que me crie y tengo el manga completo. Me gustan mucho los juegos de cartas, aunque no tengo tiempo para aprender otro más, por lo que un CCG que no me pide jugar, solo coleccionar, la verdad es que me entra muy bien. Personalmente, tanto por acabado como por propuesta, sí que me merece la pena. Es un nuevo álbum que me está dando gusto completar, pero al final todo depende de gustos. Si disfrutas del coleccionismo y el anime de Naruto es uno de tus preferidos, merece mucho la pena, y es que la calidad de sus artes es realmente llamativa. En caso contrario, quizá no sea para ti, pues no es un TCG. ¿Lo bueno? Que si Naruto ha llegado, el resto también lo harán. Y hay mucho entre lo que elegir.

articles.title: How Rockstar Made Every NPC Feel Alive in GTA 6
articles.summary: Rockstar made NPCs feel alive in GTA 6 by "establishing deep backstories for almost everything" throughout Leonida.
articles.body:
Game developers often refer to their open world cities as characters due to the sheer craftsmanship involved in building out a believable, diverse playspace for the player with its own districts, history, and architecture. This is truer for GTA 6 than most games, but what makes Leonida really feel alive — outside of the puddles of bin juice, the regional-specific cop cars, and mapped out power grid — are the people who live there.

GTA 6 feels like a massive evolution in what it means to be a non-player character (NPC) because there’s an emphasis on the “C” — they’re actually characters in their own right. NPCs don’t just all look unique — with body types, skin, dress style, and hair making them stand apart — they have their own personalities and temperaments. Start a fight with one NPC and they might fight back, while another runs away. One could start a fight by slapping you, another might flick their cigarette at you or tip their drink over your head. Passersby can cheer the fight on, flee, or get involved. Some stop after a single punch knocks sense into them, while others swing until they’re out cold .

No matter where you go in GTA 6, it feels like a lived-in world, on the macro and micro scale. There are over 100 interiors to explore, and each house tells you a story about its occupants. Listen to conversations out on the streets and you’ll get a window into their minds, built out by an entire Rockstar studio dedicated to making them authentic and believable, while still being larger-than-life, funny, and often unhinged.

“A big part of it was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories,” said Steven Messinger, Rockstar's senior design director for the open world. “For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we’ve fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they’re distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer.

“Players will only pick up on bits and pieces of this, but having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren’t there.”

To build this tangible sense of place, Rockstar takes in-depth research trips for GTA games , embedding the writers in the mundane and the more extreme to really capture the soul of a city. Helicopter trips of the Florida Keys, ride-alongs with police, talking to people, taking photos and notes, all build up a snapshot that Rockstar bottles up to digitize in video game format.

“We had a lot of fun trying to capture the raw energy and vibrant chaos that Florida is known for,” said senior design director of world and population, John Macpherson. “By immersing ourselves into a number of these locations on reference trips, spending time with locals, experiencing as much as possible firsthand, we gathered a direct sense of what would make Leonida feel truly alive.

“Everywhere you look, little stories constantly unfold. It could be as simple as what someone’s wearing, how fit they are, how they walk and talk, who they’re with, what tunes they’re blasting as they cruise down the street. We tried to match that in-game as much as possible, hopefully resulting in something that feels full of life.”

You can walk along Vice Beach and see sugar daddies with their trophy wives, locals playing volleyball, tourists sunbathing, and people walking their pets. Everywhere you look, there’s something happening in Leonida, and it’s completely enveloping. You feel like a part of its world, rather than a godlike being with total control over it.

There’s a mission around the midpoint of the game where protagonists Jason and Lucia people-watch from a hotel sunbed, inventing backstories for the guests by the pool, and it’s something I found myself doing as I explored the world and passed people by, such is the variety and diversity of the game’s NPCs. No other game has ever had such a colorful cast of extras, which is wild when you consider all this was built to add credibility to a world you can zoom past at 100mph.

“We evolved from monolithic NPCs built to visual standards that were lower than the main cast in GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, to fully fleshed-out characters with singular awareness and visual identities,” said Valmor Garcia, senior technical art director on GTA 6. “They are driven by dynamic moods, personalities, unique anatomy, facial features, and dialogue that are visually on par with our protagonists, Jason and Lucia.”

Rockstar built entirely new technology for GTA 6 to simulate hair, cloth, and the way muscles move under the skin. All that work is implemented equally across all characters, so there’s never that uncanny moment where you come face-to-face with a flat and lifeless NPC, staring at you with dead eyes. Everyone you meet is equally detailed, and the range of visual design is staggering.

Of course, this approach created challenges in other areas of development. It’s fairly straightforward to implement a combat system in a game where all character models are approximately the same size, but the varied body types of GTA 6 meant Rockstar had to take a look at how it approached animations so physical contact looks good no matter how big or small the character models are. Especially since this is a game where the two leads can also change in size through diet and exercise .

“We decided early on that we wanted to really push the variation in character sizes and body types,” vice president of animation, Mark Tennant, explained. “This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat.

“Developing this workflow meant that we needed our animators to adopt new techniques compared to a more traditional approach. We also had to grow a team dedicated to overseeing the implementation, which required close collaboration with the art and rigging teams. All these aspects needed to come together to make it work, so it was a huge team effort.”

It wasn’t just player-on-NPC contact that needed to be considered either. There are dozens and dozens of scripted scenes dotted about Leonida to find, the usual Strangers and Freaks of Rockstar games weaved into the fabric of the world, manifesting as wacky encounters of various size and scope. Some are one-on-one, but sometimes you become a spectator as two NPCs with opposing goals clash. If you decide to intervene, the game has to account for every possible permutation of that.

“Shifting the centre of action off the player at times required a lot of careful thought too — if a cop is doing a stop-and-search on another criminal in the world, how do they behave if you commit a crime in front of them?” vice president of design Stephen Donkin explained. “Do they switch their attention to you? Do they compare the severity of the crime? If they come after you, what does the original criminal do? Does he drive off? What happens if you follow him?

“Every event, encounter, interaction had to be considered with this level of depth, as there are so many possible inputs to any given situation, and every new feature or mechanic that is added becomes a new input we must collectively consider.”

It’s astounding that Rockstar managed to keep this level of detail consistent over a full playthrough. Even 140 hours in, I’m still seeing new things and being blown away by the level of reactivity in every facet of the world, from Jason’s “mmm, chicken” when he kissed Lucia while she was tucking into off-brand KFC, to the police calling off a stop and search because I pulled my in-game phone out to record them.

GTA 6 is a towering achievement made by a development team of perfectionists, and we likely won’t see anything quite like it until Rockstar does it again.

articles.summary: Just like in real life, there are some people you really shouldn’t mess with in GTA 6. It’s not always easy to tell at a glance either. Books, covers, and all that.
articles.body:
Just like in real life, there are some people you really shouldn’t mess with in GTA 6 . It’s not always easy to tell at a glance either. Books, covers, and all that.

GTA 6 has a wild range of NPCs with unpredictable and unique behavior — you never know what you’re gonna get. Players have been documenting their adventures across Leonida and their interactions with the locals, and have come across the weird, the funny, and the downright scary.

Not only do some NPCs fight back, but they fight hard and can take more punches to the head than Rocky. Some of them even bring little friends along to the throwdown.

The viral clip below, from @WIZZYGM , shows Lucia attempting to take someone’s car. Instead of allowing themselves to be dragged out, however, they got psyched up about having a tussle. They were into it.

Not only did they take a ridiculous number of punches directly to the nose, but at one point they even gave Lucia some free shots. Then they banged some powder up their snout and Hulked out. He even took a gunshot straight to the head!

Nah this Npc’s got it 🔥🔥🔥 #GTAVI #GTA6 #ViceCity. — WIZZY🔫⚽️ (@WIZZYGM) November 20, 2026

Nah this Npc’s got it 🔥🔥🔥 #GTAVI #GTA6 #ViceCity.

“I appreciate that the NPCs in this game act like true Floridians,” read one reply . “Bro said ‘I can run faster than you can drive’ nah son im turning the game off lmfaooooo,” said another .

In another clip, from @chrisdadeviant , Jason attempts to hijack a car but the person inside had a massive meltdown and started headbutting the steering wheel, honking the horn with each forehead slam. Eventually, she got out and threatened to stomp Jason’s teeth out of his head.

Jason ignored the temper tantrum and got in the car anyway, and she tried to pull him out before he drove away. Here’s the clip for that one:

😭😭😭😭😭😭😭 — chris (@chrisdadeviant) November 20, 2026

“This is such a valid crashout lmaooooooooo,” said one fan . “Yea just let her keep the car, she clearly going through something,” another joked .

One clip going around is downright terrifying. The player, having found a sniper rifle at the top of a tower, wanted to test their aim. They looked through the scope at an NPC, took aim, and fired a shot directly at their chest.

Instead of falling over, the NPC started walking towards the tower. Blood pooled on their clothing where the bullet landed, more shots rang out and landed right on target, and they kept coming, tucking their drinks under the arm and breaking into a full sprint.

On the way, they were hit by a car and shot multiple times. There was a trail of blood marking out their route, but they just kept coming.

A similar clip showed a player sniping an NPC. The NPC saw them aiming and mimicked a slice across the neck with their thumb, before tanking bullets and sprinting at the player. Eventually, they teleported behind the player and attacked.

THIS GTA 6 NPC CAN SOMEHOW SPOT YOU AND TELEPORT BEHIND YOU TO ONE-SHOT YOU 😳💀 #GTA6 #GTAVI #GTA — Millzaa (@Millzaatv_) November 20, 2026

THIS GTA 6 NPC CAN SOMEHOW SPOT YOU AND TELEPORT BEHIND YOU TO ONE-SHOT YOU 😳💀 #GTA6 #GTAVI #GTA

It’s not just people you have to watch out for either. In one clip, a player hijacked a car, thought they were safe, and then heard noises from behind them. It was the vehicle’s owner’s cat in the back seat, which jump-scared them and savaged them with claws and teeth.

In GTA 6, Jason steals a man’s car with a cat in the backseat. While driving, the cat jumps on him, and he throws it out of the car before continuing to drive. — GTA 6 Updates (@gtasix_) November 18, 2026

“Nah I’m sold this is crazy I can’t wait to play,” said one reply . “Best game of all time bro,” another posted .

Clearly, Rockstar has tuned some NPCs to give the player a hard time, so keep your wits about you! If you're interested in how Rockstar made the game feel so alive, we have comments direct from the GTA 6 development team on the creation of its many NPCs .
